proposals.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (about 6 eV), Li-rich phosphate that is electrochemically insulating and oxidatively stable near 4 V. Its P(V)-O chemistry is close to the PS4 framework of Li6PS5Cl, so the expected interface reactivity with the sulfide is limited, and it is a known protective coating on LiCoO2. This is a first evaluation, so no prior result motivates it.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a fully reduced, Li-rich oxide with no P(V), S-reducible or halogen-oxidizable centers. Its O2- anion is already at the most reduced oxidation state, so it should have very little driving force to oxidize the PS4/Cl framework of Li6PS5Cl, unlike Li3PO4 (P(V) gave SO2/P2O5 products, penalty 0.337) and LiF (penalty 0.310, where the reaction still released S/SCl species). Its wide band gap should keep it insulating.
proposal.motivation: Both prior contacts (Li3PO4 at 0.337 and LiF at 0.310) still had sizable reaction penalties, so the next choice should move to an even more reduced, Li-saturated anion chemistry that avoids both the oxidizable P(V) center and the fluoride-driven reaction pathway.
